name: BAL, sputum and bronchial washings
use: Infection, BAL differential count, malignancy screening (use WHO Lung categories for malignancy).

adequacy.title: Adequacy
items: BAL: few bronchial cells (<5% suggests alveolar sample); differential count on cytospin.

categories.name: Benign / descriptive patterns
criteria: BAL differential (normal: macrophages >80%, lymphocytes <15%, neutrophils <3%, eosinophils <1%).

diagnoses.name: Lymphocytic BAL
diagnoses.comment: Sarcoidosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, drug reaction; CD4:CD8 ratio if available.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Eosinophilic BAL
diagnoses.final: BAL with eosinophilia (>25% suggests eosinophilic pneumonia).
diagnoses.comment: Eosinophils >25% supports acute or chronic eosinophilic pneumonia; consider drugs, parasites, ABPA, EGPA.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Neutrophilic BAL
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Haemosiderin-laden macrophages
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
diagnoses.final: Foamy alveolar casts; GMS shows Pneumocystis.
diagnoses.comment: Foamy alveolar casts on Pap; GMS shows cup-shaped cysts. Typically HIV/immunosuppressed; PCR/IF where available.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Lipid-laden macrophages
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Asbestos bodies / Curschmann spirals / Charcot–Leyden crystals
diagnoses.comment: Asbestos bodies (beaded ferruginous fibres) indicate exposure; Curschmann spirals indicate small-airway mucus (asthma, COPD); Charcot–Leyden crystals indicate eosinophil breakdown.
diagnoses.cat: Suggested template category: Benign / descriptive patterns

diagnoses.name: Malignant cells in BAL/sputum
diagnoses.final: Malignant cells present – [type] (WHO Lung category: Malignant).

extra.title: Status
items: Consensus/descriptive – no official international reporting system.

references: WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology. IARC, 2022.
Meyer KC, et al. An official ATS clinical practice guideline: the clinical utility of BAL cellular analysis in interstitial lung disease. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2012;185:1004–1014.
